key_insight: CLEF HIPE-2026 defines a standardized evaluation for extracting person–place relations from noisy, multilingual historical texts, emphasizing both accuracy and runtime efficiency when distinguishing 'at' (ever been) vs 'isAt' (located around publication time).
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of benchmarks and shared tasks for robust person–place semantic relation extraction in noisy OCRed, multilingual historical corpora across different time periods and language varieties.
method: Organize an evaluation lab with multilingual, time-stamped annotated datasets and clear relation definitions ('at' vs 'isAt').
Provide baseline systems, standardized metrics (accuracy, precision/recall, and efficiency/runtime), and guidelines for handling OCR/noise and temporal context.
Encourage approaches combining multilingual modeling, temporal reasoning, and lightweight/efficient inference to trade off accuracy and speed.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to benchmark and improve robust, efficient relation-extraction systems for historical and archival text, benefiting digital humanities, provenance analysis, and large-scale historical knowledge base construction.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input (noisy OCR text) → preprocessing (cleanup, language detection) → relation classifier → output (at / isAt labels).
World map or language timeline illustrating multilingual corpora and time periods covered.
Precision/recall vs inference time plot to highlight accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.
Confusion matrix comparing 'at' vs 'isAt' errors to show common failure modes.
paper_title: CLEF HIPE-2026: Evaluating Accurate and Efficient Person-Place Relation Extraction from Multilingual Historical Texts
paper_authors: Juri Opitz, Corina Raclé, Emanuela Boros, Andrianos Michail, Matteo Romanello
